items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: I don't think there were any other blacks that I knew of that had been working in film, other than Phil Bill Moore and Calvin Jackson

ctx.x: They were not encouraged to feel that people were going to be calling on them?

I guess -- I guess that's the feeling, you know; you wonder how much time can you put into this and what can you look forward to, you know, and as long as I had the band, I sort of felt that I should hold on to that for a little security, although I wanted to write for pictures, and at that time, there, -- gee, I don't think there were any other blacks that I knew of that had been working in film, other than Phil Bill Moore and Calvin Jackson, who had come to California with Harry James to work on a picture at MGM.
There were no blacks in the studio orchestras. You know.
